title: Stability Duty Rotation — Weekly Briefing & Triage Notes
content:
Date: 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-05
Owners (rotation): Dana Liu (primary), Aisha Kumar (backup)
Attendees: Dana, Aisha, Ben, Carlos, Erin (brief), Felix (ops check-in)
Channel: #release-duty (standup at 10:00 PT daily)
---
Purpose: weekly handoff notes for the stability/on-call rotation. Capture triage outcomes, decisions for the upcoming release train window, emerging risks, and quick runbook edits. This is a working doc (informal) — keep short bullets.

Summary (top line):
- Production latency percentile drift on token-serving path stabilized after last night's kernel revert; follow-up audit required.
- One regression candidate identified in model-variant routing that increases tail latency under burst; mitigation = throttle-to-legacy-route for affected customers.
- Minor config drift in canary autoscaler policy (scale-down cooldown reduced incorrectly) — fixed and PR created.

Agenda/Notes by day:
2026-03-02 (kickoff)
- Observed increase in 99th p50->p99 gap at 23:05 UTC.
- Immediate action: rolled back runtime-kernel v7.3 -> v7.2 on canary cluster to stabilize.
- Data: token QPS unchanged; CPU tails rose, GPU utilization steady -> points to scheduling/kernels.
- Owner: Carlos to gather kernel perf traces and upload to S3 (s3://redwood-diagnostics/stability/2026-03-02).

2026-03-03 (triage)
- Trace analysis: contention on fused-attn kernel when sequence-length distribution spikes.
- Short-term mitigation: adjusted request routing weight to favor pinned instances during evening burst windows.
- Decision: do NOT roll out kernel v7.3 to dedicated pools this week.
- Owner: Ben to mark rollout hold in release planner and notify Solutions Eng.

2026-03-04 (canary + config)
- Canary autoscaler cooldown mismatch found (prod autoscaler had cooldown 60s, canary 15s due to a templating bug).
- PR created: runtime/infra#2321 — fixes templating and adds unit test.
- Owner: Erin to shepherd PR and coordinate deploy; expected merge 2026-03-06.

Decisions and rationale:
- Hold on kernel v7.3: risk of tail latency regressions outweighs perf gains for average. Need more microbench coverage for varied seq-length distributions.
- Canary windows tightened to low-traffic slot (03:00–05:00 PT) for next two nights.
- Hotfix policy for this rotation: if p99 latency increases >25% for more than 30 minutes and error-rate >0.5% -> trigger emergency rollback and notify on-call lead.

Action items (with owners and ETA):
- Carlos: upload kernel traces + flamegraphs to S3 and link to ticket (RELEASE-421). ETA: 2026-03-03 EOD.
- Ben: flag kernel rollout hold in release planner + message Solutions Eng + Sales (customers with dedicated pools). ETA: 2026-03-03 done.
- Erin: land runtime/infra#2321 and coordinate canary redeploy. ETA: 2026-03-06.
- Dana: update runbook section 'kernel-regression' with rollback checklist and test commands. ETA: 2026-03-05.
- Aisha: author quick postmortem template for any hotfix triggered this week; include token counts and per-tenant impact table. ETA: 2026-03-07.
- Felix: add alert refinement for fused-attn contention (new metric: fused_attn_queue_length_p95). ETA: 2026-03-05.

Risk matrix (quick):
- High: model-variant routing change (probable) -> symptom: p99 spike; mitigation: throttle to legacy route, increase canary scrutiny.
- Medium: autoscaler template drift -> symptom: oscillation during scale-down -> mitigation: template tests + staged rollout.
- Low: disk-pressure on warm caches during bursts -> symptom: cache miss tail -> mitigation: increase cache buffer ephemeral size for night windows (temporary).

Canary and rollout notes:
- Canary window: night low-traffic 03:00–05:00 PT.
- Canary target: small shard group (shard-08, shard-09) + subset of internal test accounts only.
- Canary health criteria: p50/p95 within 10% baseline, p99 within 15%, no increase in 5xx beyond 0.2 percentage points.
- Rollback triggers: p99 > 15% or 5xx increase >0.5% for >15 minutes or sustained queue growth metric.

Hotfix thresholds & playbook (abridged):
- Detection: auto-alerts + on-call manual triage.
- First 10m: gather traces, pin suspected component, toggle to safe route if available.
- 10–30m: attempt config-based mitigation (disable feature flag, reduce batch sizes).
- >30m meeting: declare hotfix path, cut hotfix branch, notify legal/GTM if customer impact > X (use Aisha's template).

Observability checklist to verify pre-rollout:
- Trace sampling at 100% for canary shards for first 20 minutes.
- Ensure KV cache hit-rate dashboards show > 92% baseline.
- Verify rollout metric hooks are wired: route-weight, queue-length, fused_attn_queue_length_p95.

Runbook edits (notes to self):
- Insert example curl commands for manual rollback in 'release-runbooks/stability-duty' page.
- Add link to kernel microbench harness and instructions to run locally (devbox).
- Add checklist line: "Confirm PR includes unit test for templated values".

Customer comms (if needed):
- Draft notice if dedicated customers see degradation: keep messaging technical + reassuring; offer a timeline and mitigation steps. Template: short email + scheduled call. Owner: Ben + Solutions Eng.

Follow-ups for next handoff (2026-03-06):
- Confirm PR merge and canary redeploy completed.
- Check p99 and fused_attn metric for 24h window post-deploy.
- Review kernel microbench results and decide whether to expand test coverage to mixed-seq workloads.

Unresolved/questions:
- Why did canary template drift occur only for a subset of clusters? (Possible templating cache bug) — investigate templater pipeline logs.
- Do we have runbook entries for throttling by customer-tier? Add explicit command snippets.

Quick notes / scratch (informal):
- "If we keep toggling kernels, need to add canary label to change history so we can filter events quickly."
- "Remind infra: add safe-mode flag between routing and model-selection to bypass new routing logic."

Appendix: Helpful links and diagnostics
- Perf traces: s3://redwood-diagnostics/stability/2026-03-02/trace.tar.gz
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2321
- Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RELEASE-421
- Runbook: confluence://release-runbooks/stability-duty

End of note.
